</TreeView>

examples.code:
<TreeView
  aria-label="Files"
  selectionMode="single"
  defaultSelected="src/App.tsx"
  defaultExpanded={['src']}
>
  <TreeView.Item value="src" label="src" icon="folder">
    <TreeView.Item value="src/index.ts" label="index.ts" icon="file" />
    <TreeView.Item value="src/App.tsx" label="App.tsx" icon="file" />
    <TreeView.Item value="src/legacy.ts" label="legacy.ts" disabled />
  </TreeView.Item>
  <TreeView.Item value="package.json" label="package.json" icon="file" />
</TreeView>

accessibility:
`TreeView` follows the [APG Tree View Pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/).

- **Roles:** the root is a `<ul role="tree">`, each item an `<li role="treeitem">`, and an open
  parent's children sit in a `<ul role="group">` inside it. A closed item's children have no
  markup.
- **A name:** a tree needs one, from `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and a development build
  warns when it has neither. Each item is named by `aria-labelledby` pointing at its own label, and
  declares its `aria-level`, which VoiceOver needs according to
  [GitHub's testing](https://github.blog/engineering/user-experience/considerations-for-making-a-tree-view-component-accessible/).
  `aria-expanded` is on parents only.
- **One tab stop, with real focus:** one item holds `tabIndex={0}` and the rest `-1`, and focus
  moves from item to item, rather than through `aria-activedescendant`. When focus comes into the
  tree, it lands on the selected item, or in a checkbox tree on the first checked item on the page.
  Without one, it lands where focus last was, or on the first item. If the item holding the stop
  goes away, its nearest ancestor on the page takes it, and focus goes too if it had focus.
- **Selection:** a `single` tree marks each enabled item `aria-selected`, `true` or `false`. A
  `checkbox` tree marks `aria-checked` on every item, `true`, `false` or `mixed`, disabled ones
  included, and adds `aria-multiselectable="true"` to the tree. A tree never has both, and a tree
  with no `selectionMode` has neither. Selection doesn't follow focus.
- **The box** is a [`Checkbox`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/form/checkbox) inside an `aria-hidden` span, with
  `tabIndex={-1}`, so it's neither a tab stop nor a second thing for a screen reader to read. The
  item's `aria-checked` is what a screen reader hears.
- **Disabled items** are `aria-disabled` and stay reachable from the arrow keys, Home, End and
  typing, so a screen reader user finds them. They're never selected, checked, opened or closed.
  One that's already open stays open, so what's under it is still reachable.
- **A loading item's row** is a `treeitem` that says Loading…, marked `aria-disabled` and reached
  the way a disabled item is, so a screen reader user who moves into the folder hears what's
  happening. It has no value: it's never selected or checked, it has no `aria-selected` or
  `aria-checked`, and a checkbox tree doesn't count it. If it goes with focus on it, focus moves to
  the item it was loading for. Bulma's loader turns in its chevron's place, hidden from assistive
  tech.
- **A failed load's row** is a `treeitem` named by its message and the Retry button's text, such
  as "Couldn't load src Retry". Enter, Space or a click on the row calls `onRetry`, in every mode.
  The button is drawn inside an `aria-hidden` span and takes no focus, the way an item's box is,
  so the tree keeps its one tab stop, and nothing in the message should be a link or a button
  either. A retry that starts loading keeps the same row, so focus stays on it. With no `onRetry`,
  the row is disabled and shows the message alone.
- **Announcements:** a visually hidden `role="status"` region with `aria-live="polite"` sits right
  after the tree, one for the whole tree, from the moment it mounts, so a screen reader is already
  listening when something is written into it. It says "Loading src" when an open item starts
  loading, a failed load's message, and "src loaded" when the loading row or a failed load's row
  goes with the item still open.
  The name is the item's label as a screen reader reads it. A closed item, or one in a closed
  branch, says nothing. Each announcement is written a moment after the change and cleared soon
  after, so the page doesn't keep a second copy of the text.

Enter and Space do the item's one thing, which depends on the mode:

| Key   | No `selectionMode`       | `single`         | `checkbox`               |
| ----- | ------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------ |
| Enter | Opens or closes a parent | Selects the item | Opens or closes a parent |
| Space | Opens or closes a parent | Selects the item | Checks or unchecks it    |

On a failed load's row, both retry, whatever the mode. The rest work the same in every mode:

| Key        | What it does                                                                              |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Down, Up   | The next or previous item on the page, without wrapping                                   |
| Right      | Opens a closed parent, and focus stays. On an open parent, moves to its first child       |
| Left       | Closes an open parent. Otherwise moves to its parent                                      |
| Home, End  | The first item, and the last one on the page                                              |
| `*`        | Opens every closed parent beside the focused item, itself included. Focus stays           |
| Characters | Moves to the next item whose label starts with what's typed, several characters adding up |
| Tab        | Leaves the tree                                                                           |

- **Right to left:** Right and Left swap in a right-to-left page, and the chevron points to the
  left while closed.
- **Keys it leaves alone:** anything with Control, Alt or Meta held, anything while an input method
  is composing, and Escape, so it reaches a Modal or Popover around the tree. An item's own
  `onKeyDown` runs first, and calling `preventDefault()` there keeps the tree from acting on the
  key.
- **Clicks:** the chevron only opens and closes. The rest of the row does the item's one thing:
  opens or closes it with no `selectionMode`, selects it (and opens or closes a parent) in a
  `single` tree, and checks it in a `checkbox` tree. A click moves focus and the tab stop to the
  item.
- **Not for site navigation:** APG's own
  [navigation tree example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/examples/treeview-navigation/)
  says "A pattern more suited for typical site navigation with expandable groups of links is the
  disclosure pattern", and a tree's items aren't links. Keep a sidebar on [`Menu`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/components/menu).
- **Focus and the selected look differ:** the focus ring sits outside the row, so it shows on the
  selected fill as well as on a plain row.
- **Forced colors:** in Windows high contrast mode the selected row is the system's Highlight and
  HighlightText, a disabled row or a loading one is GrayText, and the focus ring, the chevrons and
  the guide lines stay visible, since they're outlines and borders. A mixed box keeps its dash, and
  the loader's ring stays open.
- **Motion:** the chevron turns with a short transition, and the loader spins. Both stop when the
  reader asks for reduced motion, and the loader stays drawn.
summary: The `TreeView` component renders a tree of items you browse and pick from, the way a file explorer works: one tab stop, the arrow keys to move, and Right and Left to open and close. It's the APG Tree View pattern, drawn to look like Bulma's menu. It isn't for site navigation: items aren't links, and a sidebar whose sections open and close is `Menu`'s job. The root owns which items are open, through `expanded`, `defaultExpanded` and `onExpandedChange`. `selectionMode` picks one of three trees. With `none`, nothing is picked. With `single`, one item is, and `selected` says which. With `checkbox`, each item has a box, a check reaches every enabled item under it, closed branches included, and a parent with some of its items checked is mixed. `selected` is read in a `single` tree only, and `checked` in a `checkbox` tree only. Selection never follows focus. Disabled items stay reachable from the keys, so a screen reader finds them. The tree needs a name, from `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and a development build warns when it has neither.

props.name: children
props.description: `TreeView.Item`s, nested inside each other for their children. Render an item's children whenever you have them, open or not: the tree hides them while it's closed.

props.name: selectionMode
props.description: `none`: nothing is picked, and Enter and Space open and close a parent. `single`: one item, picked with Enter, Space or a click. `checkbox`: any number, checked with Space or a click. A check reaches every enabled item under it, and a parent with some of them checked is mixed.

props.name: selected
props.description: The selected item's value when you hold the state, or `null` for none. Read with `single` only. Picking an item then only calls `onSelectedChange`, and nothing changes until you pass the new value.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: The item selected to begin with, when the tree holds its own state. Read with `single` only.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Called with the value of the item picked. Not called for the one already selected, and moving focus never calls it.

props.name: checked
props.description: The checked items' values when you hold the state. Read with `checkbox` only. A value checks its item, and an enabled item also counts as checked when any item above it is in the list, so a parent's value stands for its whole branch, loaded or not. A disabled item is checked only by its own value.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: The values checked to begin with, when the tree holds its own state. Read with `checkbox` only.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Called after a check or an uncheck with every item that now shows checked, parents included, plus any earlier value that matches no item the tree knows, left as it was. The order means nothing. Passed back as `checked`, the list shows the same boxes.

props.name: expanded
props.description: The open items' values when you hold the state. A value stays in the list while its item's parent is closed, so the item reopens as it was.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: The items open to begin with, when the tree holds its own state.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Called with the new list whenever an item opens or closes, `*` included.

props.name: size
props.description: The text size, as Bulma's menu sizes it. The rows, the indent and the chevron scale with it.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What the row in a loading item's group says. In your app's language.

props.name: retryLabel
props.description: The Retry button's text on a failed load's row. In your app's language.

props.name: loadingAnnouncement
props.description: What the live region says when an open item starts loading, built from the item's name. In your app's language. Default: `` `Loading ${name}` ``.

props.name: loadedAnnouncement
props.description: What the live region says when that load finishes. In your app's language. Default: `` `${name} loaded` ``.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

extraProps.name: aria-label
extraProps.description: Names the tree, such as "Files". A tree needs a name, so pass this or `aria-labelledby`, and a development build warns when it has neither.

extraProps.name: aria-labelledby
extraProps.description: The id of a visible heading or label that names the tree, in place of `aria-label`.

parts.catchAll: All standard <ul> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: One item in the tree: a row with its chevron, its box, its icon and its label, and, while it's open, a group of the items under it.

props.name: value
props.description: **Required.** Identifies the item in `selected`, `checked` and `expanded`. Unique in the tree.

props.name: label
props.description: **Required.** What the row shows, and the item's name for assistive tech. Nothing in it should be a link or a button: a tree item does one thing, and nothing else in its row takes focus.

props.name: icon
props.description: A picture before the label: an `Icon` name, or a node. Hidden from assistive tech.

props.name: children
props.description: `TreeView.Item`s under this one. Render them whenever you have them, open or not: the tree hides them while it's closed, and a checkbox tree needs them to know what a check reaches.

props.name: hasChildren
props.description: Shows the item as a parent before its children are known, such as a folder that loads when it opens.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Its children are on their way. While it's open, its group ends in a row that says so, and the tree's live region says it's loading, then that it's loaded once this goes back to `false`. A parent only: pair it with `hasChildren`, or with the children it already has.

props.name: loadError
props.description: Its children didn't load. While it's open, its group ends in a row with this message, and a Retry button when there's an `onRetry`, and the live region reads the message out, so name the item in it ("Couldn't load src"), then says it's loaded once this goes with the item still open. A parent only, like `isLoading`. Nothing in it should be a link or a button: the row is what's pressed. `isLoading` wins while both are given.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Called by the Retry button on a failed load's row, and by Enter or Space there. Set `isLoading` while the retry runs, so the live region says it's loading, and reads the message out again if it fails again. The same message passed a second time with no loading between is no change the tree can see.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Reachable with the arrow keys, Home, End and type-ahead, so a screen reader finds it, but never selected, checked, opened or closed. One that's already open stays open.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.
